```{r}
# Librerias
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggfortify)  #for plotting timeseries
library(dplyr)
library(forecast)
library(lubridate)
library(readr)
library(patchwork)
```


```{r}
# Cargo datos
d <- read_excel("Agbarometer202601.xlsx")

# Preparo datos

# Creo columna con el nombre de los meses
meses <- c("Ene", "Mar", "May", "Jul", "Sep", "Nov")
d <- d %>% 
  mutate(
    Mes = factor(c('Oct', 'Nov',                       # 2018
            meses,                                     # 2019
            "Ene", "Abr", "Jul", "Sep", "Nov",         # 2020
            rep(meses, times = 5),                     # 2021 - 2025
            "Ene"                                      # 2026
            ), 
                 levels = c("Ene", "Feb", "Mar", "Abr", "May", "Jun",
                            "Jul", "Ago", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dic")),
    Año = as.numeric (c( rep("2018", times = 2),
                         rep("2019", times = 6),
                         rep("2020", times = 5),
                         rep("2021", times = 6),
                         rep("2022", times = 6),
                         rep("2023", times = 6),
                         rep("2024", times = 6),
                         rep("2025", times = 6),
                         "2026"))
  )

```


Step 3: Preliminary (exploratory) analysis.

Always start by graphing the data.

Are there consistent patterns? 

Is there a significant trend? 

Is seasonality important? 

Is there evidence of the presence of business cycles? 

Are there any outliers in the data that need to be explained by those with expert knowledge? 

How strong are the relationships among the variables available for analysis? Various tools have been developed to help with this analysis. These are discussed in Chapters 2 and 3.

# Grafico de la serie

```{r}
# Creo serie y (agbarometer)
y <- ts(d$`Ag Barometer`,
        start = c(2018, 6),
        frequency = 6,
        class = "ts")


# Gráfico serie
ggplot(d, aes(x = Bimestre, y = `Ag Barometer`)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkgreen") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
#  geom_point(color = "red", size = 2) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = "Tiempo", 
       y = "Ag Barometer") +
  theme_bw()
```



```{r}
# Test de Portmanteau
options(scipen = 999)
Box.test(y, lag = 10, type = "Ljung-Box")
```

Test de Portmanteau, p-value = 0.000000000000002887 $\cong 0 \quad \forall lag$

Q: en q parte del informe desarrollo los test? Portmanteau...


# Graficos para explorar posible estacionalidad


```{r}
# grafico de los fideos por anio superpuestos (para ver estacionalidad)
ggplot(d, aes(x = Mes, y = `Ag Barometer`, group = Año, color = factor(Año))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  labs(x = "Mes",
       y = "Ag Barometer",
       color = "Año") +
  scale_color_discrete(labels=unique(d$Año)) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
# distribucion de los datos de la serie para cada mes. ¿el promedio de los datos es el mismo para todos los meses?

# promedio de la serie fijando el mes (para ver estacionalidad)

d %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Mes, y = `Ag Barometer`)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "point",
               color = "red",
               size = 3) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Mes",
       y = "Ag Barometer") +
  theme_bw()
```


# ACF

```{r}
# ACF
ggAcf(y, lag.max = 60) +
  labs(x = "Retardo", 
       y = "FACM",
       title = NULL) + # hay q poner esto si o si, si no me pone "Series: z"
  theme_bw() 
```


# PACF

```{r}
# PACF 
ggPacf(y, lag.max = 60) +
  labs(x = "Retardo",
       y = "FACPM",
       title = NULL) +
  theme_bw() 
```
